paper_metadata.title: Quantum Quantitative Trading: High-Frequency Statistical Arbitrage Algorithm

summary: The paper proposes a fully theoretical gate-based quantum workflow for high‑frequency statistical arbitrage consisting of (1) a variable‑time preselection algorithm for detecting multicollinearity with complexity O(√d κ0² log²(1/ε)) and (2) a quantum cointegration test using quantum linear regression with complexity O(d^2.5 κ^3 / δ² polylog(dκ/δ)). In a stylized U.S. stock‑market scenario with ~8000 stocks and ~1.2×10^7 time points, the authors argue the classical workload (~10^18 operations) could be reduced to ~10^8 operations under idealized quantum assumptions requiring >50 qubits and qRAM.

experiments.description: Quantum statistical arbitrage preselection using variable-time preselection and quantum condition number comparison to identify multicollinear stock portfolios before cointegration testing.

algorithm.variant: Variable Time Preselection Algorithm (VTPA) with Quantum Condition Number Comparison Algorithm (QCNCA)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Historical stock prices are loaded into qRAM as |j⟩|t⟩|z⟩ -> |j⟩|t⟩|z ⊕ p_t^(j)⟩; portfolios are represented as matrices and converted to a Hermitian block matrix A = [[0, X],[X^T, 0]] for condition-number testing.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Preselect portfolios with condition number kappa >= kappa_0, i.e., detect multicollinearity / small eigenvalues as a proxy for potential cointegration.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Threshold-based filtering via repeated condition-number comparison; portfolios below threshold are discarded.

problem_instance.description: High-frequency statistical arbitrage over portfolios of stocks using historical quote data.

dataset_specification.description: No specific ticker list or date range given; example uses 8000 stocks, 6.5 trading hours/day, half-second quotes, 253 trading days/year.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prices stored as bit strings in qRAM; portfolios loaded as amplitude-like superpositions over time and stock indices.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity analysis; no empirical benchmark runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: qRAM loading of historical prices; construction of Hermitian block matrix from portfolio data.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical decision on whether to keep/discard portfolios after quantum threshold test.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup; from O(N^2 d) to O(sqrt(d) * kappa_0^2 * log(1/epsilon)^2)
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical benchmark for statistical arbitrage / matrix factorization preselection
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming qRAM access and uniform condition-number distribution for the stated simplified bound
speedup_claims.caveats: No hardware experiment; advantage is theoretical and depends on condition-number distribution and qRAM assumptions.

speedup_claims.factor: from O(N^3) to O(sqrt(d) * log(1/epsilon)^2 * sum_j 4^j j P_j)
speedup_claims.caveats: Average complexity depends on the distribution P_j; uniform distribution yields the simplified O(sqrt(d) * kappa_0^2 * log(1/epsilon)^2) bound.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(d) kappa_0^2 log(1/epsilon)^2) for uniform condition-number distribution; more generally O(sqrt(d) log(1/epsilon)^2 sum_j 4^j j P_j)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N^2 d) benchmark for the overall statistical arbitrage task; O(N^3) for matrix factorization in preselection

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not quantified; advantage assumes very large N (~10^7 time points) and qRAM access
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: >50 logical qubits plus efficient qRAM storing ~10^7 time-series entries; fault‑tolerant phase estimation and Hamiltonian simulation circuits
limiting_factors: Requires large-scale qRAM to load historical price matrices
Algorithm relies on block-encoded matrix access and Hamiltonian simulation assumptions
No explicit constant-factor resource estimates for fault-tolerant implementation
Condition-number dependence κ0^2 may be large in financial datasets
No empirical validation on simulator or hardware

notes: No actual hardware or experimental run is reported; this is a theoretical algorithm paper. The qubit count is estimated in the discussion (about 35 for initial state, more than 50 for VTPA), not tied to a specific device.
Authors claim complexity reduction from classical O(N^2 d) or O(N^3) style procedures to O(sqrt(d) κ0^2 log(1/ε)^2) for preselection, but the work is purely analytical with no implementation.

experiments.description: Quantum cointegration test for preselected stock portfolios using quantum linear regression followed by a classical Augmented Dickey-Fuller-style residual test.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Cointegration Test Algorithm (QCT) with two-stage quantum linear regression

hyperparameters.kappa: condition number of regression design matrix

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Amplitude-encoded design matrix and target vector are loaded from historical stock data; first regression estimates coefficients beta, then residuals are formed classically and used in a second regression on time and lagged residuals.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Test whether a linear combination of stock prices is stationary/cointegrated via Engle-Granger two-step method; compute regression coefficients beta and ADF test statistic DF_T = gamma_hat / SE(gamma_hat).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Classical comparison of the test statistic with critical values from a Dickey-Fuller table.

problem_instance.description: Cointegration verification on stock portfolios after multicollinearity preselection.

dataset_specification.description: No specific tickers or date range given; uses historical price matrix X and target vector y.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Residuals computed as u = y - X beta; lagged residuals Delta u_t = u_t - u_{t-1}; then second regression on time trend and lagged residuals.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity analysis; no empirical runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical matrix multiplication, vector subtraction, and Dickey-Fuller critical-value comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical residual construction after quantum regression; classical computation of standard error and test statistic.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare DF_T with critical value table to decide cointegration.

results.value: O(d^2.5 * kappa^3 / delta^2 * poly(log^2(d * kappa / delta)) + dN + (L+2)^2.5 * kappa'^3 / delta'^2 * poly(log^2((L+2) * kappa' / delta')))
O(d^2.5 * kappa^3 / delta^2 * poly(log^2(d * kappa / delta)))
results.unit: asymptotic complexity of first quantum linear regression

results.value: O((L+2)^2.5 * kappa'^3 / delta'^2 * poly(log^2((L+2) * kappa' / delta')))
results.unit: asymptotic complexity of second quantum linear regression

classical_baselines.method_name: classical matrix multiplication and vector subtraction

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup in d and N for the regression subroutine; quantum regression replaces classical residual-generation scaling
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical residual generation and matrix operations
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming qRAM access and well-behaved design matrices with singular values in [1/kappa, 1]
speedup_claims.caveats: The full cointegration test is hybrid; classical postprocessing remains necessary for residual construction, standard error, and Dickey-Fuller comparison.

speedup_claims.factor: quantum linear regression complexity O(d^2.5 kappa^3 / delta^2 poly(log^2(d kappa / delta)))
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical runtime or hardware validation reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(d^2.5 kappa^3 / delta^2 poly(log^2(d kappa / delta)) + dN + (L+2)^2.5 kappa'^3 / delta'^2 poly(log^2((L+2) kappa' / delta')) )
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not given as a single explicit asymptotic bound for the full cointegration test; residual generation by alternative classical-style method cited as O(N log N kappa^2 epsilon^-3)

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not quantified; depends on very large regression problems with large N and moderate d
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault‑tolerant implementation of quantum linear system / regression algorithms (HHL-style) with qRAM access to the design matrix and target vector
limiting_factors: Relies on quantum linear regression derived from HHL with strong assumptions (well-conditioned matrices, efficient oracle access)
Requires qRAM for amplitude encoding of financial time-series data
Hybrid algorithm still requires classical residual construction and statistical testing
No empirical resource counts or hardware demonstration

notes: This is also a theoretical algorithm with no hardware execution. The paper explicitly states the second stage is hybrid: quantum regression plus classical matrix multiplication, subtraction, and test-statistic computation.
Paper claims polynomial complexity improvements for regression-based cointegration testing using quantum linear regression, but provides only asymptotic analysis without implementation.
